title: ArrayBlockingQueue versus LinkedBlockingQueue
context: How do ArrayBlockingQueue and LinkedBlockingQueue differ?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java collections questions (1 of 2)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Both are thread-safe bounded or unbounded queues where producers wait when the queue is full and consumers wait when it is empty. ArrayBlockingQueue uses a fixed-size array and one lock for both ends. Its capacity is fixed at construction. LinkedBlockingQueue uses linked nodes and two separate locks, one for put and one for take, so producers and consumers contend less. It is unbounded unless you give a capacity. Choose ArrayBlockingQueue for a strict bound and predictable memory.

points.title: One lock versus two
points.why: LinkedBlockingQueue lets a producer and a consumer work at the same time.

points.title: Capacity
points.why: Always set a bound on a blocking queue in production, to avoid unbounded memory growth.
